author: Elastic
rule.description:
Detects a ChatGPT Enterprise user downloading five or more distinct Google Drive files through the Drive connector
within a one-hour window. Adversaries who abuse a linked Drive connector after session compromise often stage bulk file
retrieval before sharing, forwarding, or other exfiltration.
false_positives:
Users exporting or reviewing many Drive files through ChatGPT during approved research, eDiscovery, or migration
    work.
rule.name: OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise Google Drive Download Burst
rule.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise Google Drive Download Burst

One user retrieved five or more distinct Google Drive files through ChatGPT in an hour. That pattern can indicate bulk
collection via the Drive connector ahead of exfiltration.

Escalate when downloads follow sensitive Drive searches, Gmail discovery or sends, or unusual authentication activity.
Close as a false positive for approved bulk export or research projects.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Review `Esql.download_count`, `Esql.download_url_values`, and the time bucket on the alert.
- Correlate with nearby Google Drive sensitive query bursts or Gmail connector activity from the same user.
- Confirm whether Drive connector downloads are approved for that user and volume.
- Check subsequent conversation shares or external forwarding of the retrieved content.

### False positive analysis

- Migration, eDiscovery, or research workflows may download many Drive files in a short window through an approved
  connector.

### Response and remediation

- Revoke Drive connector access if unauthorized and inventory downloaded files for data exposure.
- Hunt for follow-on shares, Gmail sends, or additional downloads from the same user in the surrounding window.
rule.setup:
## Setup

This rule requires the OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise integration to collect `app_log` events for Google Drive, including
request logs with flattened `openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.input` fields `download_raw_file` and `url`.

https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/openai_chatgpt_enterprise
rule.query:
from logs-openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log-*
| where
    data_stream.dataset == "openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log" and
    openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.app_name == "Google Drive" and
    openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.log_type == "request" and
    openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.input is not null and
    user.email is not null
| eval
    Esql.download_raw_file = to_lower(field_extract(openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.input, "download_raw_file")),
    Esql.download_url = field_extract(openai_chatgpt_enterprise.app_log.input, "url"),
    Esql.time_bucket = date_trunc(1 hour, @timestamp)
| where Esql.download_raw_file == "true"
| stats
    Esql.download_count = count_distinct(Esql.download_url),
    Esql.download_url_values = values(Esql.download_url),
    Esql.timestamp_first_seen = min(@timestamp),
    Esql.timestamp_last_seen = max(@timestamp)
  by user.email, Esql.time_bucket
| where Esql.download_count >= 5
| keep
    user.email,
    Esql.time_bucket,
    Esql.download_count,
    Esql.download_url_values,
    Esql.timestamp_first_seen,
    Esql.timestamp_last_seen
